name: Greek red-figure pottery
summary: Greek vases in which the background is black gloss and the figures keep the red of the clay. The painter draws the inner lines with a brush, so the figures look rounder and freer.

philosophy.core_thesis: A vase is a field for the drawn human body: the figure stays the colour of the clay and the brush line gives it weight, movement and feeling.
design_principles: Reserve the figures in the red clay and paint the whole ground in black gloss.
Draw the inner lines with a brush in relief lines, thick and raised, for the main contours.
Use thinner dilute lines for muscles, hair and folds of cloth.
Show the body in three-quarter view, twisted and foreshortened.
Frame the picture with a meander or a palmette border, and a plain black wall below.
Place one or two figures in the tondo of a cup so that the circle holds the pose.
Fire in three stages, oxidation, reduction and re-oxidation, to fix black and red.
anti_patterns: Black silhouettes with incised detail on a red ground
Flat profile figures that do not turn
Thick opaque added colour over the large areas
A crowded frieze with no black field
A glazed surface with clear gloss over the red

form.shape: Kraters, amphorae, hydriai, lekythoi and kylikes with a thin, elegant wall and a clear profile.
form.profile: A smooth S-curve with a distinct neck; a kylix has a shallow, wide bowl on a short stem.
form.foot_and_rim: A moulded foot ring or a stem, a thin lip, and handles that follow the form of the neck.
form.proportion: Height 20 to 55 cm, wall 2 to 5 mm, and the picture field about half of the height of the body.
rules: Throw the wall thin and even, so that the picture sits on a clean surface.
Set the picture where the form is widest and nearest to the viewer.
Paint the base ground black, leave a reserved line under the picture.
Keep the handles slim and let the black slip cover them.

bodies.rule: Use a very fine Attic clay with iron that fires to a clear orange-red. The clay must be free of grit, so that the brush line stays sharp.

methods: throwing in parts on the wheel
turning the foot and the lip
forming.joins: Parts are joined with slip when the clay is leather-hard; the joins are smoothed under the black paint.
forming.details: Raised relief lines, a faint preliminary sketch in the clay, and a stilt mark under the foot.

glaze.pattern: One main scene of myth, athletics or daily life in reserved red, framed by a meander, a palmette or a wave border.
glaze.gloss: The black ground is glassy, about 70 to 85 GU; the reserved clay is satin.
glaze.wear: The black may flake on the lip and the edges; the line drawing stays crisp.

palette.strategy: Two fired colours, a deep black ground and the red clay, with white and yellow-brown only as a small accent.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired updraught kiln with a controlled flue and green wood for the reduction phase.
processes: draw the sketch in the leather-hard clay
paint the black ground and the lines
firing.scale: Workshops in the Kerameikos of Athens made thousands of vases, with a master painter and a team.
firing.signs: Raised lines that stand up from the clay, a bright black field and a faint sketch under the paint.

pieces.form: Calyx krater with a wide mouth and one large scene between the handles
Kylix with a round tondo of one figure and a black exterior
Neck amphora with a single figure on each side on a black ground
Hydria with a domestic scene on the shoulder and a palmette below

positive: orange-red figures on glossy black ground
museum photograph on a neutral ground

evidence.title: Red-figure kylix by the Brygos Painter
Calyx krater signed by Euphronios, Louvre
Red-figure calyx krater with Nike and a tripod

emotion.target_response: A quiet, humane poise: the viewer sees a body drawn with a free line and feels a moment of real movement.

use_cases: a museum label for classical Greek vases
a figure scene on a cup or a krater
an educational image of Greek daily life on pottery
avoid_when: the brief needs a glazed finish or a white body

modifiers.how: Reverse the ground: paint the figures in black slip on red clay and cut the details with a point.
Remove the painted figure, keep the fine red slip, and mould the relief into the surface.
